title: Andrew, McKenzie and Gore named in West Indies A squads
text:

Caribbean linkages’ • CUB chairman named as director amidst FTX fallout • Revised minimum wage likely to take effect on New Year’s Day • Advertisement --> Advertisement The Big Stories Andrew, McKenzie and Gore named in West Indies A squads By Observer Desk - October 28, 2026 at 11:35 pm - 0 Advertisement --> Advertisement Share this story Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Instagram By Neto Baptiste Antigua and Barbuda’s Jewel Andrew, Micah McKenzie and Karima Gore have been selected for the West Indies A squads for the upcoming home series against England A in St Kitts and Nevis from November 1 to 16. Andrew has been named in both the 13-member Twenty20 (T20) squad and the 15-member One-Day team, while McKenzie will feature in the One-Day squad and Gore in the T20 side. Alick Athanaze will captain the T20 team, while Keacy Carty has been appointed skipper of the One-Day squad for the eight-match series. The series begins with three T20 matches at the Conaree Cricket Ground from November 1 to 4, followed by five One-Day (List A) matches at Warner Park and Conaree from November 7 to 16. The One-Day series will provide players outside the senior team with a valuable opportunity to press their claims for selection to the West Indies squad for the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup Qualifier, which begins in February. The regional side will be seeking to secure qualification for the 2027 World Cup in October. The T20 matches, meanwhile, will form part of the preparation and selection process for the 2028 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup, for which the West Indies have already qualified after reaching the Super Eight stage of the 2026 tournament. Athanaze, an emerging leader within the West Indies set-up, is the most internationally experienced player in the T20 group. He will be joined by four members of the senior squad – Vitel Lawes, Andrew, Quentin Sampson and Kamil Pooran – who will have the opportunity to sharpen their skills and improve their understanding of the format. Carty, the most experienced player in the One-Day squad, will also have the chance to demonstrate his leadership qualities while gaining valuable match practice ahead of the World Cup Qualifier. West Indies Academy player Rivaldo Clarke has earned a place in the One-Day squad following Kevin Wickham’s maiden Test call-up for the ongoing series in Bangladesh. Wickham had been in contention for selection before his elevation to the senior team. Clarke previously captained the West Indies Academy to a 2-1 victory over Sri Lanka Emerging XI in a three-match 50-over series in June. Cricket West Indies Director of Cricket Miles Bascombe said the One-Day matches would play an important role in determining the players selected for the World Cup Qualifier, while the T20 series would begin preparations for the 2028 global tournament. “The Qualifier in February is the most important assignment of our 50-over year, and we are treating it that way. Our aim is to win it and take that form to the World Cup in October,” Bascombe said. “These One-Day matches are a big part of how we choose the players to do that, and the T20 matches start the work for 2028.” Bascombe added that head coach Ottis Gibson had been tasked with clarifying each player’s role, identifying those closest to stepping up to international cricket and determining the areas in which they need to improve. Mikyle Louis, who has played 10 Test matches, will join the group throughout the series as a development attachment, focusing on improving his white-ball game within the high-performance environment. Gibson, the West Indies fast-bowling consultant and former head coach, will lead the coaching staff, supported by batting coach Rohan Nurse and spin-bowling coach Nikita Miller. West Indies A T20 squad Alick Athanaze (captain), Jewel Andrew, Zachary Carter, Shadrack Descarte, Keon Gaston, Karima Gore, Joshua James, Vitel Lawes, Zishan Motara, Jakeem Pollard, Kamil Pooran, Quentin Sampson and Stewart Thompson. West Indies A One-Day squad Keacy Carty (captain), Kevlon Anderson, Jewel Andrew, Alick Athanaze, Jediah Blades, Rivaldo Clarke, Shadrack Descarte, Jyd Goolie, Kirk McKenzie, Micah McKenzie, Vitel Lawes, Shaqkere Parris, Jakeem Pollard, Shamar Springer and Oshane Thomas.
